fix_note: 'Listen again' re-fetched the feed with no trace the click did anything — the same dispatches came back and nothing on screen changed. The click now announces 'Listening again…' above the feed and, when the fetch lands, confirms 'Dispatches refreshed · <time>'; the note clears when the world changes. First B8 record under the per-seat append regime (founder ruling 2026-11-12).

'Open a brain' now opens the brain's detail view: picking a brain (or a card's Details button) shows its corpus stats and its model-version history from the real /api/brains/:brainId/history endpoint, with honest empty states. Previously a pick only scrolled to and ringed a stats card for four seconds — and on an instance with no recorded interactions there was no card at all, so the pick landed silently on the empty state.

With Gmail not connected, the floating Compose button opened a Gmail composer onto the connect wall — a sheet that could never send (on the reported build, no visible effect). Compose (the button and the C shortcut) now routes to the player-mail composer instead: it switches to the Player mail mailbox and opens its Compose tab, exactly the ticket's expected behavior. When Gmail is connected, Compose opens the Gmail composer as before.

An over-limit post showed only a negative counter (-1630) with no explanation. The composer now says it in words beside the counter — 'N over the 500-character limit — trim to post.' — appearing the moment the text crosses the limit and clearing when it is back under; Post stays disabled while over.

Two state/feedback defects. (1) 'The Long Field' (the 95% affinity milestone) opened 'Years, now, since the vows' although it fires on affinity alone for couples with zero marriages — its first line now speaks of the first spark and the long road since, true at any marital state (the only marriage-presupposing line in the scene set). (2) Interact at the affinity cap (or floor) returned a plain ok and the UI silently refreshed to identical numbers; the engine now reports capped:true and the desk answers with a toast — 'Affinity is already at its peak with this partner.' (or 'at its lowest').

The player-mail gift and COD amount fields coerced every keystroke (a typed -1 became 01, letters became 0, and 999999999 sailed through to a server refusal). Both fields now hold the typed text and parse only at Send: a non-number, a negative, or an amount over the server's governing 1,000,000 CC bound (badNumericField, server/domains/mail.js) is refused by name under the fields — 'Gift amount must be a number from 0 to 1,000,000 CC.' — with the form kept open and the typed text untouched; a hint states the range up front. Same typed-string shape as the housing place inputs.

Mailing yourself was refused only by a red banner after Send ('You cannot mail yourself'). The composer now fetches the signed-in id on mount and explains at the recipient field the moment the picked recipient is yourself — 'That's you — player mail can't be sent to yourself, so Send stays off until you pick someone else.' — with Send disabled until the recipient changes (the ticket's explain-before-Send leg; the server refusal stays as backstop and no money/escrow semantics changed).

There was no way to start a courtship from the lens — the panel only listed existing courtships and its empty state sent users out to an NPC's context menu in the world. The Courtships panel now carries a 'Start a courtship' form: pick a player through the standing recipient search (resolved to a real account) or name an NPC met in the world, and Begin performs the first interaction — which is what creates the courtship server-side — after which it appears in the list with its affinity and Propose path. A blank partner is refused in the open with what to do; the empty state now points at the form.

Partners rendered as raw ids ('player:<uuid>', 'npc:<id>'), and a past marriage showed a bare 'player:' because the server presenters strip the other player's raw account id without putting a name in its place. Rows now carry partner_name/partner_handle resolved the way mail names correspondents: players through the users table (display name, else @handle), an NPC's id is its world-visible name, an unresolvable player carries nulls and the UI falls back to 'A Concord member' — never the raw id. All four panels (courtships, marriages, past marriages, pregnancies) plus the dissolve and heart-event modals render the shared partnerLabel. The privacy strip itself stands. Two shipped suites' raw-form expectations were updated to the name form, disclosed here. NAMED, NOT FIXED (desk's call): the same strip removes the partner id from the owner's OWN marriage rows, which the conceive/dissolve actions post back — a privacy-posture question beyond this display ticket.

The lattice Overview showed platform-wide consent corpus counts (Total rows 562,259, consented 2,868, per-table totals) with no scope label, so a regular user could read them as their own corpus. The endpoint is deliberately a public anonymized aggregate, so the surface now takes the ticket's labelling leg: a scope line under the heading states these are platform-wide totals across every creator on this instance — not just your DTUs — and points to the Consent tab for the viewer's own state; the stat cards and the per-table heading carry the platform-wide label too. No counts, endpoints, or permissions changed.

The invariant Overview's Monitors-active badge showed '70%' with 0/0 monitors: the badge carried the global lock-70 CSS class, whose ::after paints a hardcoded '70%' regardless of data. The badge no longer uses that class; it renders the real active percentage as a chip (same styling) computed from the monitor summary, and only when monitors exist — with none, the badge shows 0/0 and no percentage at all. The lock-70 class itself stays for the Home locked cards, a different surface outside this ticket.

The social Inbox badge read 25 against 75 unread in the panel: the badge (the social page's Inbox tab) read only the social-store count, while the panel counts both stores (social + the platform queue). Three legs now measure the same set: the page badge adds the platform queue's unread, mirroring NotificationBell; the panel fetches both routes' full 200 window instead of 50, so its header chip no longer undercounts past a page; and the server's getUnreadCount applies the same notification-type preference filter as getNotifications (muted types no longer inflate the badge against the list).

The goddess dispatch feed was stale and uniform — every dispatch 'I observe: the cycle continues.', ecosystem 0.00 — because composeAndRecord read the ecosystem score from STATE.worlds, which in the real server is the sub-worlds store keyed by userId (values are arrays of a user's worlds), so the worldId lookup never hit and the score was always 0. The broadcaster now reads the world's real ecosystem mean from player_world_metrics via score-engine's worldEcosystemPercent (the sanctioned reader; an empty sample is not a score) and maps it onto the tone scale, so dispatches carry the world's actual tone and score. With no metrics sample it falls back to an in-memory world object that genuinely carries a numeric score, else the previous neutral 0. Matches how viability-cycle and analytics already read the same table.

Commune replies were identical canned text for every commune type: the intent never reached the reply, so greet/petition/offering/question all returned the reception (usually greet) template. The commune action now answers the intent — an author-written dialogue template whose trigger is the intent speaks for that intent when present; otherwise a deterministic intent line derived from intent + reception + the deity's tone axes is added (a petition heard or unheard, a question answered plainly, veiled, or not at all, an empty-handed offering noted). An offering is now acknowledged whenever the deity does not refuse it, not only in the received band. All four intents produce distinct utterances, pinned by test.
